cross_package_notes.note: Informational cross-package observation (outside w1-agent-sec boundary, untouched): HostApprovals.attach reads tenantID via types.TenantIDFromContext(ctx) rather than types.CallerFromContext(ctx).TenantID (unlike mcp_tool.go:249, confirmed_tool.go:110, ask_user.go:115, secure_form.go:145, and page_tools.go:326). Safe today because Lite host tools are single-workspace, but worth keeping aligned if Lite host tools are ever exposed across shared-agent workspaces.

invariants_checked: Extension origin validation (validExtensionOrigin) strictly requires chrome-extension://<32 lowercase a-p chars> on both AuthorizeHTTP and WebSocket ServeHTTP, blocking arbitrary web page CSRF and DNS-rebinding hijacks.

Pairing and renewal token handling stores only SHA-256 hex digests in DB, enforces single-use atomic pairing exchange, requires explicit 'Bearer ' authorization header scheme, validates canonical 32-byte base64url tokens on both HTTP and WebSocket subprotocol entry points, and uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare for secret/token equality checks.

Daemon Unix socket gatekeeper enforces 0700 private runtime directories (rejecting /tmp, /var/tmp, /private/tmp), constant-time per-daemon secret verification before proxying to inner bsk socket, and 24 MiB frame bounds.
Cluster inter-node RPC verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures with hmac.Equal over timestamp + method + path + body, enforces 60s clock skew and nonce replay cache, and restricts internal forwarding URLs.
Multi-tenant and per-user Scope{Tenant, User} isolation binds device records, leases, and conversation task maps, stripping caller-supplied session_id / browser_instance_id overrides.

Navigation URL validation (navigate and tab_create) rejects dangerous schemes (file://, javascript:, chrome:, chrome-extension:, data:, devtools:, view-source:), control characters, and missing hosts before auto-starting sessions or dispatching RPCs.

WebSocket/HTTP body and screenshot preview payload bounds (ReadLimit, http.MaxBytesReader, maxFrame, preview size checks) and concurrent disconnect/pause/cancel races verified under -race; reserved BrowserSkill identifiers preserved per REBRAND_RESERVED.md with zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: Manager.Call (callLocal) forwarded params['url'] in navigate and tab_create to the local Chrome extension without scheme validation (unlike statusPageURL), allowing prompt-injected tool calls to auto-start a browser window and open file://, javascript:, chrome://, chrome-extension://, data:, or devtools:// URLs.

AuthorizeHTTP used strings.TrimPrefix(..., 'Bearer '), accepting raw tokens without a 'Bearer ' prefix and comparing token == input.NextToken non-constant-time; ServeHTTP checked len(token) != 43 instead of canonical 32-byte base64url validToken(token) before querying storage.

invariants_checked: Multi-tenant and per-user ownership binding enforced across RequestAndWait, RequestHostAndWait, RequestOAuthAndWait, AskUser, RequestSecureForm, PageAction, ResolveForResume, ResolveResponse, and ResolveSecureForm.
AnswerableKinds excludes mcp_oauth and secure_form from generic user prompt resolution so OAuth callbacks and server-side credential vault handlers remain the sole resolvers for those kinds.

Session and standing automation grant bindings hash canonical tool arguments / domains (BindingHash) and verify Risk coverage via policy.Covers so TOCTOU argument changes or risk escalations invalidate prior grants.
Single-use consumption via hitl.Broker.Consume transitions answered prompts to executing/done under owner-instance verification, preventing replay of expired, canceled, or already-consumed approvals.

Strict JSON decoding with DisallowUnknownFields and trailing-EOF rejection enforced on tool_approval, mcp_oauth, ask_user, secure_form, and page_action response validators, plus host Scope/Access clamping against proposed AllowSession and GrantAccess.

MCP policy lookups (IsEnabled, Action, ToolRisks) fail closed on missing tenant/service/tool identity or checker errors; ResumeDecision, ResumeAnswer, and ResumeSecureForm guard against nil receivers/prompts and kind confusion.

findings.summary: validateToolApprovalResponse did not validate Scope ('once'/'session') or Access ('read'/'write'), allowed Scope/Access on rejections, and ignored trailing JSON tokens (as did validateMCPOAuthResponse, which also lacked DisallowUnknownFields and required 'authorized'); furthermore, RequestHostAndWait passed client-supplied Scope='session' when AllowSession=false and Access='write' when GrantAccess='read', allowing callers on /agent/prompts/{id} to widen a read-only host grant into a write grant.

Gate.Action failed open to DeclaredRisk(tool) (allowing readOnlyHint=true tools without approval) when tenantID==0, serviceID=='', or tool identity was empty despite a configured checker; Gate.ToolRisks likewise skipped policy lookup on missing tenant/service, ignored RiskChecker.Policy when ListByService was unimplemented, and trusted readOnlyHint instead of RiskWrite when Checker did not implement RiskChecker.

RequestSecureForm and ResolveSecureForm lacked explicit non-zero TenantID and non-blank UserID guards, SecureFormPrompt lacked nil gate/broker guards, and ResumeDecision / ResumeAnswer / ResumeSecureForm lacked nil prompt and Prompt.Kind verification before unmarshaling and consuming.

invariants_checked: Broker.Resolve enforces non-zero matching TenantID, fail-close per-user UserID matching, optional SessionID/Kind scoping (returning ErrPromptNotFound to prevent cross-session probing), and registered kind response validation before state transition.

Atomic compare-and-swap transitions in MemoryStore and SQL Store guard status, owner_instance, and lease_until so concurrent Resolve, timeout, cancellation, reaper, and Consume operations never double-consume or lose answers.
Waiter channel registration and close-once wakeup broadcast via sync/Redis pubsub are race-free under concurrent Await/Resolve/Cancel/Reap.

Orphaned pending prompts with expired owner leases are reaped prior to Resolve (suspended when suspendable, expired with owner_stopped otherwise) so answers are never recorded onto dead non-suspendable prompts.

findings.summary: Broker.Resolve checked row.TenantID != req.TenantID without rejecting zero TenantIDs, allowing an unattributed request (TenantID=0) to match an unattributed prompt row (TenantID=0) instead of failing closed with ErrTenantMismatch.

Broker.Resolve only invoked reapPending on lease-expired Pending prompts when row.Suspendable was true, allowing a non-suspendable prompt whose waiting replica had crashed to transition to a permanent zombie Answered row with no waiter or suspension state.

invariants_checked: Reviewer fails closed on nil reviewer/model, empty or mismatched SessionID, missing RequestID, empty/whitespace-only current-turn user messages, incomplete wildcard targets (TargetsComplete=false), incomplete scripts (ScriptsIncomplete=true), oversized actions (>64 KiB pre-masking), oversized current-turn transcripts (>64 KiB), model timeouts, cancellations, or tool-call attempts.

Prompt serialization isolates untrusted action fields inside structured JSON, caps earlier background messages while keeping current-turn authorization messages whole, and masks secret-named environment variables before sending prompts to external review models.

Assessment parser enforces a single JSON object (optionally inside one markdown fence without trailing text), DisallowUnknownFields, trailing-EOF rejection, and requires outcome=allow with risk_level in {low,medium} and user_authorization in {medium,high}.

findings.summary: actionOf serialized req.Env values in plaintext into the external LLM user prompt (unlike tools/host_approval.go which masks secret-looking env keys on UI cards), leaking API keys, tokens, passwords, and cookies to the review model.

Reviewer.review did not reject blank turn.SessionID or mismatched req.SessionID != turn.SessionID, accepted whitespace-only current-turn user messages, and splitTranscript dereferenced nil *types.Message entries without guarding.
parseAssessment used json.Unmarshal without DisallowUnknownFields or trailing-token EOF verification, accepting malformed multi-field / unknown-key JSON replies instead of failing closed.

invariants_checked: Decide and Offered enforce read-only mutation denial, treat unknown Risk values as destructive (Ask under auto_write/confirm, Deny under read_only), and fail closed (Deny / not offered) on any non-empty malformed AssistantAccessLevel while preserving empty default confirm semantics.

Grantable restricts in-run session grants to non-Always RiskWrite actions, Pregrantable restricts standing automation grants to non-Always RiskWrite/RiskDestructive actions, and Covers requires both granted and call Risk values to be valid with call risk not exceeding granted risk.

findings.summary: Offered checked level != AssistantAccessReadOnly without validating non-empty levels via level.Valid(), causing malformed access levels (e.g. 'readonly', 'none', 'bogus') to fail open (offering mutating/destructive tools and returning Allow on read/probe); Covers also did not explicitly require granted.Valid().
